Table1.note: Counts are unweighted; percentages are survey weighted within each column and may not total 100 because of rounding. Continuous summaries are survey weighted. The 564 participants with gaps are a subset of the overall population; no between-column tests were performed. A gap requires an activity reported as needing help or impossible to perform and explicit non-receipt of help for that activity. Family assistance denotes a confirmed helper report and may coexist with a gap; other records do not establish absence of family help. ADL, activities of daily living; IADL, instrumental ADL; IQR, interquartile range; SD, standard deviation. Measurement and source-availability details are in Table S1.

Allocations to people reporting family assistance
Table2.note: S0, function-first; S1, gap-first. Both allocate 500 complete programmes per 1,000 original, survey-weighted candidates; S1 additionally pays for targeted enquiry. TableS3.title: Functional and family profiles of gainers and displaced candidates at equal 500 places
TableS3.note: The 53 gaining and 49 losing source records contribute changes in allocation probability, not simple participant averages. Each side represents 17.40 weighted opportunities per 1,000 original candidates. Profiles and CIs are weighted by allocation-probability changes. All released intervals use 5,000 valid paired community draws except recorded family-help hours for gaining records (4,974). Withheld cells and protected valid-draw counts remain undisclosed. Family-help hours are recorded assistance, not estimated time savings.

TableS4.title: Paired allocation differences across nine capacity scenarios
TableS4.note: S1 minus S0, per 1,000 original candidates; 5,000 paired community draws. Equal places assumes information already known; fixed resources charges targeted enquiry to the corresponding capacity ceilings. Structural zeros are shown as 0. Protected cells are withheld, not zero. The IADL difference is an index total, not patient deterioration. Figure 2 reverses its sign to show the need-coverage loss.

TableS5.note: Per 1,000 original candidates; costs are 2024 US$. Enquiry rows compare S1 targeted (alternative) with universal (reference) enquiry; rural fixed-resource rows compare S1 with S0. No-displacement expansion retains original S0 opportunities and adds complete programmes. Rural restoration compares S1 resources for 500 programmes with the original ceilings, NOT rural S1 with S0. Totals add stored increments to unrounded constants; intervals are the original paired increments (or the stored package-total interval translated by 500). Rural travel adds 0.5 h to each of four nursing and six OT visits. OT binds the next-programme step in all 5,000 community and county draws; RN also binds in two county draws for S1. Money alone cannot replace staff time.

TableS6.title: Reallocation after reassessment of needs in 2020
TableS6.note: Per 1,000 original 2018 candidates. The same 1,386 observable eligible participants represent 557.16 original opportunities; half is 278.58, not 500. Reference and alternative are S0 and S1 except the explicitly labelled updating rows, which compare frozen 2018 with updated 2020 functional priority. No failures or capacity shortfalls occurred in the original 5,000 community or county resamples of these contrasts. Unknown qualification is not absence of need. Current-eligibility compatibility bounds are 557.16–632.45; they are not CIs. This is natural reassessment, not a programme treatment effect.
